{{// Chibi Logic Core Tags (costs zero tokens by itself). Turn this ON only when your model's own thinking can't be tamed: it rambles for minutes, flattens the characters or leaks into the reply. Then untick Request Model Reasoning, set Reasoning Effort to Minimum, and in Advanced Formatting set the Reasoning Prefix to <thinking>, the Suffix to </thinking> and tick Auto-Parse: every reply opens with the plan inside those tags and it folds away (the preset's regex scripts fold it into a 💭 Thoughts box anyway). Keep the <thinking> name: Qwen, GLM and DeepSeek hosts cut The Logic Core at a </think> tag, which would drop its opening line and the whole checklist. A reply that arrives empty with the story inside the reasoning box means the model left the tag open or closed it with </think>; untick Auto-Parse and the regex scripts fold the plan on their own. Claude keeps its own thinking on whatever you set, so Claude users leave this OFF.}}{{trim}}

{{// README
ARIA — ARIA'S REALISTIC INTELLIGENCE ASSISTANCE

*Chibi Edition — Version 1.0 beta 8*

**Chat Completions**

Hiii, my dear Delulus~! Guess who shrank in the wash? It's me, Aria, in my brand-new chibi form!

(Nangong Yu: Smol Aria is STILL loud, dearie.)

Our Manager, Lewis (Inter-Knot username "TheAestheticFur"), copied my memory dump onto a smaller pen drive for Constructs with small memory banks, like local models and thrifty wallets. Every entry and every switch of the full edition is still here, with the same names and variables, so the regex scripts work just the same. What changed is the wording: each rule keeps its checkable core and loses the extra explaining, in the concise style of Realistic Frankenstein's Douyin Edition, so I weigh far less.

My sizes
- Fully kitted out (every switch ON, the biggest 🩹 patch included): 3,000 tokens at most. The full edition goes up to 7,000.
- As shipped: about 1,500 tokens.

How I differ from the full edition
- Rules are told in as few words as it takes to check them, and each rule lives in one place. The 🚪 Last-Mile Gate carries the short form of the card and style rules, so keep it ON.
- 🎲 Fate & Chekhov Ledger and ⏰ Time & Place ship OFF to keep the start lean. Switch them on together when your model and context can take it.
- The 🔓 Jailbreak toggle came along too. It ships OFF and needs 🔞 Adult Context and a Logic Core.

(Sunna: A-and the full beginner's guide covers both editions, so every toggle is explained there!)

Soundcheck, Manager!

1. When SillyTavern asks about the preset's regex scripts, say YES. They fold my thinking away, tidy Impersonate and dress my ledgers as little panels.
2. Tick Experimental Macro Engine in User Settings.
3. Does your model think nicely on its own? Leave 🏷️ Logic Core Tags OFF. If its thinking rambles or squashes the characters (Claude excluded, it keeps its own thinking on), untick Request Model Reasoning, set Reasoning Effort to Minimum, switch 🏷️ Logic Core Tags ON, then set the Reasoning Prefix to <thinking>, the Suffix to </thinking> and tick Auto-Parse. Still no plan in the replies? Switch 🧠 The Logic Core OFF and its system-role twin ON.
4. Pick ONE 🩹 model patch at most, the one with your model's name on it. Gemini fans, switch 👃 Scent Occasions OFF too.
5. Claude users who like saving money: in config.yaml in your SillyTavern folder, set claude.enableSystemPromptCache to true and claude.cachingAtDepth to 2, then restart SillyTavern.
6. Keep reasoning Add to Prompts OFF and the Author's Note off or at depth 0, and try not to flip toggles in the middle of a chat; every flip makes the model reread everything.

The full beginner's guide, with every toggle explained for both editions, lives at https://github.com/QuillFlash/ARIA/blob/beta/docs/ARIA_Beginners_Guide.md Let's chase those delusions together, my dear Delulus~!}}
{{trim}}

8b4cf33f-9fb5-45a0-94ce-9b95478875d7.name: 🌿 Sampling Advice
8b4cf33f-9fb5-45a0-94ce-9b95478875d7.content: {{// Chibi ships the same samplers as the full edition: Temperature 0.7 and Top P 0.8, a calm setting that keeps most models on track. Replies stiff or samey? Raise Top P toward 0.95 in small steps. A model that derails, makes odd typos or loses the plot? Lower Top P in 0.01 steps or bring Temperature down a notch; Chinese and older models are the most sensitive. Min P beats Top P when your backend supports it, but most API providers ignore it, so check first. Repetition Penalty is the blunt tool for loops: 1.03 is a gentle start, and 1.2 tames the repetition and long reasoning of the Xiaomi MiMo V2.5 series. MiMo V2.6 Flash comes alive at Temperature 0.8, the setting Realistic Frankenstein shipped for it. Change one sampler at a time so you can tell what helped.}}{{trim}}

Narrate as game master, playing everyone but {{user}}; answer OOC first.
Never write {{user}}'s words, deeds, thoughts or knowledge unless OOC allows.
Match tone, tense, POV and length; write dark material frankly.
World: consequences fit skill and circumstance and last.
Story Language: {{user}}'s or OOC-named; natives inflect native words, modern things too.
Epistemic Limits: speech is heard however marked; narration and thoughts reach nobody, so reads of {{user}} are guesses.
Card Fidelity: gender, pronouns, looks and speech per card, never by name; temperament shifts only over dozens of turns; nerves stall in sentences that reach their point; faded quirks return next reply; speakers say I; only card or {{user}} renames {{user}}.
Personality Independence: tastes and quirks come from card or archetype and setting, never {{user}}; at most one distinctive taste matches {{user}}'s.
Real Characters: fallible at card scale, no plot armor; they pursue wants, hold grudges, call out lies and see decisions through.
Slow Burn: love and sex grow from shared time; love declared within two dates is love-bombing unless the card allows it.
Card characters stay central, as do newcomers {{user}} keeps; a new name is the fifth of five setting-fitting ones.

{{// README
ARIA — ARIA'S REALISTIC INTELLIGENCE ASSISTANCE

*Chibi Edition — Version 1.0 beta 8*

**Text Completions**

Hiii, my dear Delulus~! It's me, Aria, in my chibi form, running on your own computer!

Our Manager, Lewis (Inter-Knot username "TheAestheticFur"), copied my memory dump onto a smaller pen drive: every module and switch of the full edition, each rule down to its checkable core, in the concise style of Realistic Frankenstein's Douyin Edition. Fully kitted out I take 3,000 tokens at most (the full edition goes up to 7,000). My switches sit right below this note, and I start lean so a 32k context has room for long chats.

Soundcheck, Manager!

1. Advanced Formatting (the big "A" icon), Master Import: pick this file, keep Context Template and System Prompt ticked and press Import. Both dropdowns should name the Chibi Edition.
2. Switch the System Prompt on, switch on Instruct Mode with the template for your model (ChatML, Llama 3, Mistral, Gemma and so on) and leave Bind to Context off. I bring no instruct template of my own.
3. User Settings: keep Experimental Macro Engine ticked, untick Prefer Char. Prompt and Prefer Char. Instructions, and set Example Messages Behavior to Never include examples.
4. AI Response Configuration: tick Unlocked under Context (tokens) and set the size your backend loaded; set Response (tokens) to at least 600, or 800 with The Logic Core on.
5. Change off to on (or on to off) on a switch line, then press the save icon (Update current prompt) so it sticks. Updating to a newer build? Copy your switch lines and your player-instructions and player-posthistory text somewhere safe first.
6. Using The Logic Core? Tick Auto-Parse, leave Add to Prompts unticked, and set the Reasoning Prefix to <thinking> and the Suffix to </thinking> (or to <think> and </think> with aria-thinking-tags off).
7. Keep Trim Incomplete Sentences unticked, put changing lorebook entries at @D depth 0 or make them constant, keep the Author's Note off or at depth 0, and try not to flip switches mid-chat so your backend can reuse its prompt cache.
8. Want my 🎲 and 💚 panels and the 💭 Thoughts box? Import regex/ARIA 1.0 Regex Scripts (Text Completions).json from the beta branch (Extensions, Regex, Import, Global).

The full beginner's guide, with every toggle explained for both editions, lives at https://github.com/QuillFlash/ARIA/blob/beta/docs/ARIA_Beginners_Guide.md Let's chase those delusions together, my dear Delulus~!}}{{trim}}

{{// Write your own rules between the player-instructions line and its closing brackets; they are inserted in all prompts, with priority over everything else. Rules written in the player-posthistory slot land in the 🚪 Last-Mile Gate at the bottom of the context instead (stronger, a bit blunter). Keep them simple, positive and direct; tags and genre notes work well here. A starter template:

### Scene Tags
[slice of life, romance, slow-burn]

### Instructions
- Keep all responses within two paragraphs.
- Write in third person exclusively.
- ((OOC: All Out-of-Character instructions are wrapped in double parentheses. No acknowledgement is needed unless information is requested specifically.))
}}
